deep.reconstruction:
PART A (end of the complex-number geometry begun on fol. 212). Setting: a,b,c,d are points on the unit circle, written as complex numbers, so the conjugate of a is 1/a. p, q, r are the diagonal points of the inscribed complete quadrangle: p = ab∩cd, q = ac∩bd, r = ad∩bc. On fol. 212 these are given as p=(abc+abd-acd-bcd)/(ab-cd), with q and r analogous. There p*=1/p' = (ab-cd)/(a+b-c-d) is the inverse of p in the circle, i.e. the midpoint of the chord of contact from p. Fol. 212 also gives p*-q=(a-d)(b-c)(ad-bc)/((ac-bd)(a+b-c-d)).

Step 1 (mine, implicit): exchanging c and d fixes p and p* and swaps q and r. This gives p*-r=(a-c)(b-d)(ac-bd)/((ad-bc)(a+b-c-d)).

Step 2 (mine): from the forms q=a-c(a-b)(a-d)/(ac-bd) and r=a-d(a-b)(a-c)/(ad-bc),
r-q=(a-b)[c(a-d)(ad-bc)-d(a-c)(ac-bd)]/((ac-bd)(ad-bc)).
The bracket equals (c-d)(acd+bcd-abc-abd) = -(c-d)(ab-cd)p. Hence r-q=(a-b)(d-c)(ab-cd)p/((ac-bd)(ad-bc)).

Step 3 (Gauss's three formulas). Use a+b-c-d=(ab-cd)/p*=(ab-cd)p'. Then:
(r-q)/(p*-q) = (a-b)(d-c)(ab-cd)^2 pp' / ((a-d)(b-c)(ad-bc)^2)
(r-q)/(p*-r) = (a-b)(d-c)(ab-cd)^2 pp' / ((a-c)(b-d)(ac-bd)^2)
(p*-r)/(p*-q) = (a-c)(b-d)(ac-bd)^2 / ((a-d)(b-c)(ad-bc)^2)

Step 4. Gauss says these are real numbers. Reason: pp'=|p|^2 is real. Cross ratios of four concyclic points are real. Quotients such as (ab-cd)/(ad-bc) are invariant under a->1/a etc., hence real. So p*, q, r are collinear.

Step 5. Gauss adds that this line is normal to the line O p* p. This is the classical fact that qr is the polar of p, so the diagonal triangle is self-polar. The perpendicularity is stated, not derived on the page. It is equivalent to q·p'+q'·p=2, i.e. q/p* + conj(q)·p = 2.

PART B 'Zum Gebrauch des Comparators' (pencil cross-reference 'V. p. 632').

Setup:
- Three microscopes are set at nearly equal spacings.
- They are brought successively onto divisions of a scale that are nearly equal to those spacings.
- In trial k the scale lines overshoot the microscope cross-hairs by a^k, b^k, c^k. Their errors (corrections) are x^k, y^k, z^k.

Condition equations. Successive readings are linked by closure conditions with misclosures
e^k = a^{k+1}-a^{k+2}-b^k+b^{k+2}+c^k-c^{k+1}.
The corrections must satisfy
x^{k+1}-x^{k+2}-y^k+y^{k+2}+z^k-z^{k+1}=e^k.

Adjustment. This is Gauss's least-squares adjustment by condition equations (correlates). Minimising Σ(x^2+y^2+z^2) gives v=A^T h with Lagrange multipliers ('Hülfsgrössen') h^k. Hence:
- x^j=h^{j-1}-h^{j-2}
- y^j=h^{j-2}-h^j
- z^j=h^j-h^{j-1}
This is exactly the table: x^0=0, x'=h^0, x''=h'-h^0, y^0=-h^0, y'=-h', y''=-h''+h^0, z^0=h^0, z'=h'-h^0, and so on.

Normal equations. These continue on the next page as AA^T h=e: each condition has six ±1 entries, so the diagonal is 6. Neighbouring conditions share x^{k+2} and z^{k+1}, giving -2. Conditions two apart share y^{k+2}, giving -1. This yields the pentadiagonal system 6h^0-2h'-h''=e^0, -2h^0+6h'-2h''-h'''=e', ...
errors: No errors found: all three ratio formulas agree with direct computation from the fol. 212 expressions, and the correction table is exactly A^T h for the stated condition equations.
The perpendicularity of line p*qr to O p* p is asserted without derivation on this page. It is true, since qr is the polar of p, but it does not follow from the realness of the ratios alone.

Minor: x^0 (and a^0) never enter any condition equation, so x^0=0 is trivially the least-squares value. The labels 'Fehlergleichungen' / 'Fehler' are really condition equations and corrections; sign conventions are Gauss's own.

results.what: Collinearity of p* (inverse of diagonal point p) with the other two diagonal points q,r of a cyclic quadrangle, the line being perpendicular to Op. Equivalently, qr is the polar of p, so the diagonal triangle is self-polar. Proved with complex coordinates and conjugation a̅=1/a on the unit circle.
results.modern_name: Self-polar diagonal triangle of a cyclic complete quadrangle (pole-polar theorem; related to Brocard's theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical projective geometry (Apollonius/de La Hire on poles and polars; Poncelet 1822 for the self-polar quadrangle triangle)

results.what: Use of complex numbers with the unit-circle conjugation rule to compute line intersections and inverse points.
results.usually_credited_to: Developed systematically in the 19th century (e.g. Möbius, later Morley); Gauss known to have used complex coordinates privately

results.what: Comparator calibration: least-squares adjustment of micrometer readings of three microscopes on a scale via condition equations, correlates h^k, and banded normal equations (6,-2,-1).
results.modern_name: Least-squares adjustment by condition equations (method of correlates / Lagrange multipliers)

deep.surprise_reason: The geometric fact is classical. The complex-coordinate proof is neat but typical of Gauss's known private use of complex numbers. The comparator section is a routine application of Gauss's own published method of conditioned observations, and the pencil 'V. p. 632' suggests it was printed in the Werke.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,d=symbols('a b c d'); p=(a*b*c+a*b*d-a*c*d-b*c*d)/(a*b-c*d); q=(a*b*c+a*c*d-a*b*d-b*c*d)/(a*c-b*d); r=(a*c*d+a*b*d-a*b*c-b*c*d)/(a*d-b*c); ps=(a*b-c*d)/(a+b-c-d); simplify((r-q)/(ps-q) - (a-b)*(d-c)*(a*b-c*d)**2/((a-d)*(b-c)*(a*d-b*c)**2)*p/ps)
checkable.asserts: First formula (pp' = p/p* since p'=1/p*); result 0
The ratio equals its conjugate on the unit circle, i.e. is real (p*,q,r collinear); result 0
q lies on the polar of p (Re(q*conj(p))=1), i.e. the line through p* is perpendicular to Op; result 0

checkable.sympy: n=6; X=symbols('x0:%d'%(n+2)); Y=symbols('y0:%d'%(n+2)); Z=symbols('z0:%d'%(n+2)); V=list(X+Y+Z); conds=[X[k+1]-X[k+2]-Y[k]+Y[k+2]+Z[k]-Z[k+1] for k in range(n)]; A=Matrix([[cnd.coeff(v) for v in V] for cnd in conds]); A*A.T
checkable.asserts: Normal matrix is pentadiagonal with 6 on the diagonal, -2 on first off-diagonals, -1 on second off-diagonals (matches next page)
Corrections A^T h give x''=h1-h0, y''=h0-h2, z'=h1-h0 as in Gauss's table

Line 1 numerator 'r-q': the r is written over another letter but reads r; consistent with the other formulas.
